html:
Shivaji was the founder of the Maratha kingdom in western India, born in 1630 at the hill fort of Shivneri. From a small family estate near Pune he built a state that defied both the sultans of Bijapur and the Mughals.

His method was the hill fort and the fast raid. He seized forts in the steep Western Ghats one by one, and his light cavalry struck far and fled before slow armies could catch it. Key moments:

  • 1659: he killed the Bijapur general Afzal Khan at a meeting below Pratapgad and routed his army.
  • 1664: he sacked Surat, the richest Mughal port.
  • 1666: called to Aurangzeb's court in Agra, he was held under guard and escaped, by legend hidden in a fruit basket.
  • 1674: he was crowned Chhatrapati, king, at Raigad.

He set up a council of eight ministers, used Marathi in government and built a navy and sea forts on the Konkan coast. He died in 1680. His son Sambhaji was killed by Aurangzeb, but the Marathas fought on and grew into the Maratha Confederacy. Shivaji is a hero across Maharashtra today.
